# Extract the Shared Core

When several deliverables consume the same input, make the shared part a real package with tests and
reduce each deliverable to a thin script over it — instead of twelve directories each with its own
copy of the parser.

## The instance

Nine of twelve labs in [[python-programming-laboratories]] read the same Apache access log. Rather
than twelve parsers, there is one `weblog` package — `entry`, `reader`, `stats`, `config`, `cli` —
installed with `pip install -e`, exposing a console script, and each lab is a script that imports it.

> "# Only the later laboratories need these; the core package has no dependencies."
> — Python-Programming-Laboratories/pyproject.toml, 2026-07-25

The core declares `dependencies = []`; every library lives in an optional `labs` extra. A shared core
that drags a dependency tree behind it is not shared, it is imposed. See
[[setuptools-and-pyproject]] and [[zero-dependency-no-build-step]].

## What makes the extraction actually work

- **The core has no I/O.** `stats` never prints; config is read in `main()`. Had the computation
  rendered its own output, every lab would have needed a fork with different formatting and nothing
  would have been extractable — [[separating-computation-from-io]].
- **The core is the only tested code.** All six [[pytest]] files target `weblog` plus two labs; the
  thin scripts are not tested because there is nothing in them to test. Concentrating the tests where
  the logic is concentrated is the direct payoff.
- **The hard problem is solved once.** The quoted-field regex in
  [[common-log-format-parsing]] is subtle enough that twelve copies would mean eleven wrong ones.

## The honest caveat

The README frames extraction as the design — nine labs share a log, therefore one package. The commit
history **cannot confirm it**: all twelve commits landed on 2026-07-25 in strict layer order, package
first, so whether `weblog` existed from lab 02 or was extracted later once the duplication became
obvious is unrecoverable. See [[import-finished-work-into-git]]. **TODO:** unresolved;
`confidence: low` on the chronology, `confidence: high` on the end state.

## Contrast

[[discrete-mathematics-laboratories]] does the opposite and is right to: its six labs share no input,
so each is self-contained. The pattern applies when the labs share *data*, not merely a course.
[[farely]] and [[optimization-methods]] apply the same move at product scale — a pure engine shared
across hosts, a solver shared across two programs.
